brief: JPM's Oct 14 afternoon note frames two questions: the bond-yield reversal and how long the tech selloff runs. Hotter-than-expected September core CPI (unrounded 0.335% m/m vs Street's 0.2% and Feroli's 0.18% estimates) pushed October hike odds from about 20% to about 50%, then back down to roughly 32-33% as 2Y yields fully reversed intraday. JPM econ (Reinhart) forecasts core PCE at 0.31% m/m, firm enough to put October in play but still expects the next hike in December. SPX fell 1.1%, NDX 2.0%, and RTY 1.9% and is now in a correction, 11% below its peak. The initial selloff was CPI-triggered but tech-led, with SOXX down a sixth straight day on AI financing and IPO-timeline concerns, and CoreWeave bonds moved into distress as the stock fell 15.5%. Positioning data (TPM at the 46th percentile, up from the 19th in late July) leaves room for further de-grossing, but JPM stays constructive and sees a possible dip-buying opportunity. BAC missed and fell on weak trading revenue, down 5% y/y against peer growth. JPM reiterates its Tactically Bullish view into earnings, with the Monetization Menu still favoring Tech and Cyclicals and no longer pairing the Tech long with an RTY short.
